subject: Dedicated capacity: SKU mix recommendation for Hyperlytics deal
messages:
From: Alex Khan <alex.khan@hyperlytics.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing for Dedicated GPU pool — Hyperlytics

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, we're narrowing in on Redwood Dedicated for our inference tier and need guidance on SKU selection. High-level details: 

- Workloads: mix of text generation (LLM-based personalization) and large-scale embedding indexing for search/ranking.
- Models: primary model family is Llama-3 70B family for generation; embeddings use a distilled 2B family.
- Average sequence length (generation): ~1,000 tokens; 95th percentile: ~2,000 tokens.
- Peak QPS: ~120 concurrent generation requests, average 35 QPS. Embeddings: batch loads at 200k/day, realtime embeddings ~18 QPS.
- Requirements: strong KV-cache support (session affinity), predictable p99 latency for critical endpoints (~ <300ms), and cost predictability for an initial 12-month committed plan.

We'd like a recommendation on H100 vs A100 vs L4: where to use each SKU in a Dedicated pool, memory tradeoffs (KV cache pressure), and expected throughput implications. Also please flag any operational constraints (e.g., cold-starts, model quantization concerns) that would affect rollout.

If helpful, I can share our workload spreadsheet. Looking to finalize sku mix ahead of a procurement window at the end of May.

Best,
Alex
Alex Khan
CTO, Hyperlytics
alex.khan@hyperlytics.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Khan <alex.khan@hyperlytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated GPU pool — Hyperlytics

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the timeline. Appreciate the workload numbers; that helps a lot. Attaching a short template you can fill if you want to share per-endpoint QPS and token distributions.

High-level guidance up front (short answer):
- L4s: cost-efficient for embeddings and small/medium models, excellent for low-cost bursty serving of distilled models and non-KV workloads.
- A100 (80GB): good middle ground — supports larger KV caches and larger batch sizes for stable throughput at decent cost.
- H100 (80GB): best for sustained high-throughput generation on 70B-class models when you need maximum half/FP8 perf and memory headroom for long contexts.

Key tradeoffs to consider: memory pressure (A100/H100 both available in 80GB variants; L4 has less GPU memory which hurts very long-context sessions), per-card token throughput (H100 > A100 >> L4 in gen workloads), and unit-cost per token (L4 is cheapest for embeddings).

If you can send the workload spreadsheet, I'll loop in Dev (infra) and Marissa (solutions) and we'll produce a SKU-mix proposal with an estimated cost model and suggested autoscaling configuration.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachment: hyperlytics_workload_template.xlsx (spreadsheet - please populate per-endpoint QPS/token-dist)

Hi Soojin — thanks, attached the filled spreadsheet (hyperlytics_workload_profile.xlsx). Key clarifications: 

- The 120 concurrent is peak gen sessions during our morning batch window; sustained daily peak is closer to 60.
- Typical generation calls are single-turn but rely on a cached KV prefix for personalization (session KV ~ 1.6M tokens across live sessions).
- We will do occasional finetuning/adalora-style updates on a subset of models (monthly), but inference-only for most of the fleet.
- Security: must stay in our VPC with customer-managed KMS for keys. SOC2 evidence will be part of procurement.

Please let us know the recommended node mix and the expected cost delta between A100/H100-backed pools.

Regards,
Maya

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Khan <alex.khan@hyperlytics.ai>, Maya Rivera <maya.rivera@hyperlytics.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated GPU pool — Hyperlytics

Alex/Maya — thanks for the workload sheet. Looping in Dev and Marissa to propose an initial Dedicated pool allocation and operational model. Below is a short recommendation we can convert into a costed proposal and timeline. I've attached a one-page PDF (redwood_sku_reco_v1.pdf) and a quick cost sketch (cost_model_approx.csv).

Executive summary (recommended starting mix):
- L4 fleet: 30% of reserved nodes (use for embeddings + distilled 2B real-time endpoints). Rationale: L4 provides excellent per-dollar embedding throughput and lower instance cost for non-KV workloads.
- A100 80GB fleet: 50% of reserved nodes (balanced generation + KV-cache-enabled endpoints). Rationale: Good memory (80GB) for longer KV prefixes, solid throughput for 70B in fp16/INT8 quantization, cheaper than H100 for mixed workloads.
- H100 80GB fleet: 20% of reserved nodes (hot generation tier for highest throughput or large-batch transforms). Rationale: Superior raw throughput for large sequence generation and faster batch processing during peak windows.

Operational considerations and tuning:
- KV cache: Pin endpoints that use long KV prefixes to A100/H100 pools; L4 should be used only for endpoints with minimal or no KV pressure.
- Quantization: Use INT8/FP8 variants where acceptable. Note H100 shows better FP8 benefits; A100 may still be preferable where memory > compute balance is needed.
- Autoscaling: Configure steady-reserved capacity for A100 to meet p50 baseline, burst to H100 for scheduled morning peaks, and spillover to L4 only for non-KV embedding requests. 
- Rollout path: start with 3:5:2 node distribution (L4:A100:H100) for initial commit; monitor per-token latency and adjust by shifting up H100 for sustained generation p99 misses.

Estimated cost impact (very rough): using Redwood internal list price buckets and committed discount assumptions, moving 10% of generation traffic from A100->H100 improves p99 generation latency by ~20–30% at ~35–45% higher cost for that portion. L4 is ~50–60% cheaper per-embedding unit vs A100. Details in cost_model_approx.csv.

Recommended next steps:
1) Architecture review call (30–45m) with Hyperlytics infra and our ops team — schedule week of May 3.
2) Agree on committed node counts and discount tier — Redwood to produce formal quote and PO template.
3) Plan initial cutover (2–3 week provisioning + validation) once PO accepted and VPC peering/KMS setup complete.

Attachments: redwood_sku_reco_v1.pdf (one-page recommendation), cost_model_approx.csv (cost sketch)

cc: Dev — can you confirm provisioning lead times & any constraints for H100 in our us-west region? Marissa — please add the recommended autoscaling knobs to the proposal doc.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Quick infra notes:
- H100 availability in us-west: currently constrained for large bulk orders; lead time depends on commit and region; we can ring-fence capacity for a quarter with an upfront reservation.
- A100 80GB: widely available across our Dedicated clusters and the safer bet for initial baseline.
- L4: plentiful and fast to provision.
- Networking/KMS: VPC peering + customer-managed KMS support is straightforward; will need an early security onboarding (SOC2 evidence) step.

Dev Patel
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Khan <alex.khan@hyperlytics.ai>

Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated GPU pool — Hyperlytics

Soojin/Team — this is great, thanks. The 3:5:2 mix looks reasonable as a starting point. A couple quick asks before the architecture call: 

- Can you include an expected p99 latency delta estimate for the generation endpoints on A100 vs H100 for 70B at ~2k token contexts? Even back-of-envelope numbers are fine.
- For the pricing quote, please show per-node monthly and an illustrative committed tier (12 month) with the discount applied.

We'll target the week of May 3 for the architecture review. Procurement will aim to have a PO ready by May 20 if the numbers align. Also confirm SOC2 evidence cadence and whether we need an in-person audit.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alex

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Khan <alex.khan@hyperlytics.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated GPU pool — Hyperlytics

Alex — quick replies inline: 

- p99 delta (back-of-envelope): for 70B at ~2k tokens, expect p99 gen latency on A100 fp16+INT8 quant to be ~420–520ms in our baseline batch/continuous-batching config; H100 with optimized kernels and FP8 can get that down to ~320–380ms (dependent on batching window). That aligns with a ~20–30% p99 improvement when moving hot endpoints from A100->H100.
- Pricing: we'll produce the 12-month committed quote showing per-node monthly, plus the effective per-token and per-embedding unit at your expected utilization. I'll have Marissa include an illustrative tiered discount matrix.
- SOC2: we can provide the SOC2 Type II package and evidence; in-person audit is not required for standard procurement — we support third-party attestation and can coordinate an SOC2 + KMS/key-management walkthrough.

I'll send a formal quote package by EOD Tue (Apr 27) so you have it ahead of your procurement window.

Cheers — Soojin
